blocks.text: GOVERNOR OF JUDAEA · NEW TESTAMENT
Porcius Festus. He heard Paul with King Agrippa and sent him to Caesar.
RULEDi
Not given AD 59 (dates vary)
SEAT
Caesarea
HOUSE
Not stated 17th of 17 in Rome
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“Three days after he came into the province he went up to Jerusalem; he refused to send for Paul there and…”
PROPHETS
None named
ROME: 17 RULERS HEROD THE GREAT → PORCIUS FESTUS
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
Three days after he came into the province he went up to Jerusalem; he refused to send for Paul there and said the case would be heard at Caesarea. Acts 25:1–5
"Willing to do the Jews a pleasure", he asked Paul, "Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?" Acts 25:9
To Agrippa: "It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face". Acts 25:16
He found the dispute was about "one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive". Acts 25:19
"Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad." Acts 26:24
He, Agrippa, Bernice and those who sat with them agreed: "This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds." Acts 26:30–32
THE SEAT
Caesarea, where he sat
Where he held Paul's hearings
TRIALS AND HEARINGS
The hearings held
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did
Festus called the dispute "certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus". Acts 25:19
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
None. Acts dates his arrival only by Paul's 'two years' (Acts 24:27).
RAMSAY (1895)
Ramsay's date for his arrival: 59. Robertson (1915) follows it.
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 4
Acts 24 Acts 25 Acts 26 Acts 27
PASSAGES · 4
Acts 24:27 Acts 25:1–27 Acts 26:1–32 Acts 27:1
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Acts does not say how long Festus governed or how he died.
Acts does not give the letter Festus sent with Paul to Caesar.
